clue.text: Masters omitting a lot of reading?

definitions.meaning: the captain in charge of a ship or a sports team
people who skip pages leave much of a book unread

explanation.surface: A question about schoolmasters who don't bother to read much.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain of a ship is its skipper; and readers who jump over passages are, whimsically, skippers too.

clue.text: It's used with force, often in a weaker moment

definitions.text: It's used with force, often in a weaker moment

parts.words: It's used with force, often in a weaker moment
parts.note: forceful swearing is what people come out with when their self-control lapses

explanation.surface: Something applied forcefully at a point of weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing and cursing are blurted forcefully, typically when temper or restraint gives way.

parts.note: a visitor who has come up to the capital from the provinces is staying in the city

explanation.surface: Someone who has travelled up from rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London; a country visitor up for a while is in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'up' in British idiom means visiting the capital, i.e. present in the city.

clue.text: Vote taken over an Irish fish

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Someone takes a ballot about a fish from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollan is a freshwater whitefish found in Irish loughs.

parts.note: read as considering someone's sensibilities, or as a preposition meaning concerning

explanation.surface: Being considerate of another person's emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone with due regard is to show them esteem; the word also serves as a preposition meaning concerning.

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A selection of services on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a choice of services but is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a mountain range.

clue.text: He comes in to serve finally

indicators.note: comes in says one word enters another, here the pronoun goes inside the verb

parts.note: to attend on someone is to serve them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man enters to wait on table at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally means eventually, when all is over.

parts.note: read as stepping aside to dodge something, or evading an issue

explanation.surface: An order to move aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or evade, literally by a step to the side.

clue.text: Comment in a chiropody manual, perhaps

definitions.text: Comment in a chiropody manual, perhaps

parts.words: Comment in a chiropody manual, perhaps
parts.note: a note at the bottom of the page, punningly about feet in a book on foot care

explanation.surface: A remark in a handbook for foot doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: A note printed at a page's base is a comment, and chiropody concerns feet.

clue.text: Cruel as Naomi could have been on losing her daughter-in-law

parts.note: in the Bible, Ruth was Naomi's devoted daughter-in-law
losing someone leaves you without, the suffix less

explanation.surface: A biblical what-if: how Naomi would have fared had Ruth left her.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, Ruth stays with Naomi; without her Naomi would literally be 'Ruth-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means pitiless, without mercy.

parts.note: read not as a parlour but as a room for drawing in

explanation.surface: A formal reception room.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's workroom is literally a room for drawing.

clue.text: Novel shelter on the Sussex coast

parts.note: novel means new
a haven is a shelter

explanation.surface: A new kind of refuge by the seaside in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it means new. Sussex is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Newhaven is a ferry port town lying on the East Sussex coastline.

definitions.meaning: spring is one of the four times of year

explanation.surface: A springy disposition or a mood in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is a quarter of the year; and to temper something is to moderate it, as experience seasons a person.

explanation.surface: Someone is favoured, as it turns out.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy precedence over others, or simply to occur.

indicators.note: displayed by suggests the letters of the words are set out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A swimming mite shows off its skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natant' means swimming; its letters with 'mite' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is an accomplishment or skill acquired.

parts.note: covered so little that one is nearly bare

explanation.surface: Scarcely protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantily means meagrely, with little clothing.

clue.text: Such a post could be insecure

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of the word may form another arrangement

explanation.surface: A job that might prove precarious.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: a cushy, secure job is an anagram of insecure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post giving pay for little or no work.

clue.text: To him lots of things mean business

definitions.text: To him lots of things mean business

parts.words: To him lots of things mean business
parts.note: lots are items offered for sale at a sale room

explanation.surface: A busy man for whom everything is work.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller at a sale room deals in lots, numbered items for bidding.

definitions.meaning: a violin, the instrument that plays

explanation.surface: A performer to toy with.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin is a musical instrument; and to tinker idly is to play about with something.

indicators.note: outside says one word wraps around another, here the verb surrounds the pub

parts.note: let means allowed, tolerated
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A singer allowed to perform outside the local.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch prized for its song.

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone signs up for avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe to a view is to assent to it.

definitions.meaning: a slang, vulgar word for a look

explanation.surface: Appearing ordinary as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander is colloquial for having a look; and a male goose is also so called.

clue.text: Getting wed? One should know the ropes before so doing

definitions.text: One should know the ropes before so doing
definitions.meaning: joining ropes by interweaving strands needs rope skill

explanation.surface: Advice that marriage needs experience first.
explanation.definitionFit: Spliced is slang for married; and a sailor joins ropes by interweaving their strands.

clue.text: Latin spirit of strange main take to America

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the word are in an odd new order

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A Latin ghost from a strange sea is brought to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea; its letters rearranged give ANIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is the Latin word for mind or soul, used in English for hostile intent.

clue.text: Cooler measure for the aficionado 16 arrayed

definitions.text: Cooler measure for the aficionado 16 arrayed

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
a measure is an old word for a dance

explanation.surface: A cooling routine for a devotee dressed in very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is SCANTILY: the performer is scantily clad and waves fans, which cool.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque routine danced with large feather fans by a scantily dressed performer.

clue.text: Presidential address from a cathedral diocese

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A president's speech delivered from a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means a residence, not a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée Palace in Paris is the French president's official residence.

indicators.note: in places the feat within the deed

parts.note: taken as written
a feat is an exploit

explanation.surface: Surprised at a real achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confounded is to be beaten or thwarted.
